simple.meaning: פַּחַת (pachath) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a pit , especially for catching animals.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Samuel 17:9. The surrounding context includes Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פַּחַת (H6354) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: a pit , especially for catching animals
definitions.full: H6354. pachath מַּ֫חַת noun masculine 2Sam 18:17 (in 17:9 read בְּאַחַד ) pit ; — ׳פ absolute Jer 48:43 +, מָּ֑חַת 48:28 ; plural מְּחָתִים 2Sam 17:9 ; — pit , 17:9 ; 18:17 ; Jer 48:28 (Gie question text); figurative of calamity וָפ ׳מַּחַד וָפָ֑ח 48:43 compare 48:44 ; 48:44 = Isa 24:17 compare 24:18 ; 24:18 and Lam 3:47 .
definitions.rootNote: probably from an unused root apparently meaning to dig ;

occurrences.englishText: Behold, he is now hidden in some pit, or in some other place. It will happen, when some of them have fallen at the first, that whoever hears it will say, ‘There is a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom!’
They took Absalom and cast him into a great pit in the forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones. Then all Israel fled, each to his own tent.
Fear, the pit, and the snare, are on you who inhabit the earth.
